subject_group: 9.4.4 External visibility and transmitted visual indications

versions.text:
Standard: The transparency is free of distortion, optical defects, reflection, refraction, and transmissivity that result in visual aberrations. The optical properties of the entire optical path (e.g., transparency, HUDs, helmet mounted displays, and visors) from the outside world to the eye enable the pilot to perform any maneuvers within the approved operating limitations of the air vehicle, including but not limited to, taxiing, takeoff, approach, and landing. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analyze the primary pilot operations as they relate to the optical path and establish the regions of the transparency where primary operations occur. Demonstration.
  (1) Perform a demonstration on the physical air vehicle and show that the optical characteristics allow pilots to maintain visual capability. The demonstration is accomplished under day, night, and with NVDs under NVIS lighting conditions (if applicable). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
  (2) Verify in flight that the optical characteristics provide the pilots with a clear, and undistorted view, and enable them to perform all maneuvers within the approved operating limitations of the air vehicle.
